findings.title: Recreate-upgrade exit code changed from 4 to 3, breaking the documented scripting contract
findings.body: The previous release documented and implemented exit code 4 as 'Rolling Upgrade is not possible, shut down the deployment before applying the new configuration' (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE = 4). This PR reassigns 4 to FEATURE_DISABLED and changes the recreate signal to 3. The update-compatibility guide explicitly tells users not to rely on anything except the command's exit code, so existing CI/CD pipelines written against the old contract (e.g., 'if exit code == 4 then do a recreate upgrade') will silently misbehave after upgrade: a recreate-required check now returns 3 (which such scripts will treat as an unknown/error case, potentially aborting the pipeline or worse, proceeding as if rolling were possible depending on the fallback), and a disabled feature now returns 4 (which such scripts will interpret as 'recreate required'). If this renumbering is intentional, it needs an explicit callout in the release notes/upgrading guide so users can update their automation, not just a silent change in the command's own doc page.

findings.title: No test asserts the exit codes that the documentation declares as the stable contract
findings.body: The docs added in this PR (update-compatibility.adoc) present the exit code table (0 = rolling possible, 3 = recreate required, 4 = feature disabled) as the supported scripting interface, yet the tests only assert on log output. In particular, testFeatureNotEnabled asserts only the stderr message but never checks that the process actually exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), and testWrongVersions asserts the error text but never checks exit code 3. If picocli.exit(...) were skipped, mis-mapped, or a PropertyException (exit code 2) were thrown instead, all tests would still pass while the documented contract would be broken. Add assertions like assertEquals(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED, result.exitCode()) and assertEquals(3, ...) for the recreate case.
